messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — acme (acct 123456789012) is hitting intermittent NXDOMAINs for their private service mysvc.prod.acme.internal since ~30m after our AZ maintenance. Customer sees 502s from our private API gateway. They reported it immediately after we finished the maintenance window :frowning_face:

jordan_customer: Confirmed. App pods in vpc-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2) see DNS failures to mysvc. Some nodes resolve to 10.2.3.4, some return NXDOMAIN. Happens randomly. We rolled one canary and saw 50% failure rate.

sam_infra: Can you paste a dig from a failing host and a succeeding host? Also need traceroute to the resolver IP.

maria_support: Pasted what they sent —
```
# failing host (10.10.10.12)
$ dig +short mysvc.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2

# (blank) -> NXDOMAIN shown in app logs

# succeeding host (10.10.10.21)
$ dig +short mysvc.prod.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
10.2.3.4

# resolver check from control plane
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`mysvc.prod.acme.internal.`].Id'
```
messages_2:
maria_support: Also included their Route53 private hosted zone id: /hostedzone/Z0ABCDEF12345 (customer copy). They run a cross-account setup (management account has forwarding rules).

dns-bot: resolver-rule-change detected in management-account: outbound-rule rslvr-out-abc priority 100 updated 1977654200 by infra-automation

neha_sre: This looks like a split-horizon / resolver rule overlap after the automation ran. Two quick suspects: (1) Hosted zone association drift (VPC not associated with private hosted zone after automation) or (2) resolver outbound rule now points at a forwarder that sometimes returns NXDOMAIN for internal names.

sam_infra: I checked the management account records — there is an outbound resolver rule that forwards *.acme.internal to endpoint rslvr-out-abc. The VPC in the customer account is NOT listed as associated with the private hosted zone in route53 (possible automation race).

raj_oncall: Double-check SG/NACL: DNS (UDP/TCP 53) needs to be allowed to the forwarder IPs; also confirm DHCP option set (domain-name-servers) hasn't been switched to a wrong IP for some subnets. I saw a DHCP update alert during the maintenance window.

maria_support: Customer confirms DHCP option set was briefly updated by their infra automation to point at 10.0.0.3 then reverted. That lines up with flapping.

sam_infra: Immediate mitigation options:
- Reassociate the private zone to vpc-0a1b2c3d: `aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0ABCDEF12345 --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d`
- Add a temporary resolver rule with higher priority in management account that forwards acme.internal to working resolver IP (10.0.0.2)
- Roll DHCP option set change back to the stable one for all subnets (they already did partial rollback)

neha_sre: I also want to rule out cross-account hosted zone shadowing: run `aws route53 list-hosted-zones` in management and customer accounts to ensure there isn't a duplicate private zone with the same name. If there is, VPC associations can be ambiguous.

maria_support: Customer ran the list; they only have the one private zone. Management account has a forwarding hosted zone (no VPC assoc) and a resolver rule.

sam_infra: Ok — I will manually associate the hosted zone to the VPC and watch. I'll do a quick smoke tests after.

raj_oncall: I'll also validate SG/NACL logs for drops to 10.0.0.2/10.0.0.3 and check the DHCP option set history (CloudTrail) for who changed it.

maria_support: Noted — customer needs a 15m heads-up for any changes. They can tolerate a short window.

jordan_customer: Thank you. Please keep me posted, we can wait 15 minutes for the fix window.

sam_infra: Running association now (doing via CLI under my infra role):
```bash
aws route53 associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id Z0ABCDEF12345 --vpc VPCRegion=us-west-2,VPCId=vpc-0a1b2c3d --comment "emergency-assoc-1977654321"
```
Responding to this thread when complete. :eyes:

(neha_sre reaction: :thumbsup:)

sam_infra: assoc call returned ChangeInfo Id: /change/C1234567-assoc. Waiting propagation (~60s).

maria_support: Notifying customer about short maintenance window and asking them to repro after propagation.

(~~~ 90s ~~~)

sam_infra: Propagation looks complete. Verified `dig mysvc.prod.acme.internal` from previously failing host now returns 10.2.3.4 consistently. No NXDOMAIN.

raj_oncall: Confirmed no SG/NACL drops correlated with the timeframe; DHCP option set was the root cause for the partial population earlier but the missing hosted-zone association caused persistent NXDOMAIN for those hosts that used the management-forwarder.

maria_support: Customer reports 0 errors on canary post-fix. Marking as mitigated and will follow up with a postmortem.

neha_sre: Action items: (1) eng-infra to add a guardrail in automation to avoid removing DHCP option sets or dissociating VPC during rollout, (2) add monitoring alert for private-hosted-zone associations drift, (3) update runbook for cross-account resolver changes. Assign to sam_infra + infra-automation.

maria_support: Creating incident INC-2026-342 and tagging eng-infra. Will include dig/traceroute logs and the change id from Route53.

jordan_customer: Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround.

sam_infra: Filed PR to infra-automation with a validation step to check `list-hosted-zones` + `get-hosted-zone-associations` before applying DHCP/forwarder updates. Link: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/infra-automation/pull/456

neha_sre: Closing the thread once postmortem is ready. Good catch on the DHCP drift. :white_check_mark:
